title: [Bug]: openai.BadRequestError: String does not match pattern.
body:
### Describe the bug

A GroupChat with agents using OpenAI always throws the following error after 3-7 messages:
```
  File "C:\Code\AutoGen\.venv\Lib\site-packages\openai\_base_client.py", line 1064, in _request
    raise self._make_status_error_from_response(err.response) from None
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Invalid 'messages[6].name': string does not match pattern. Expected a string that matches the pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'messages[6].name', 'code': 'invalid_value'}}
```

### Steps to reproduce

```
import autogen
import os

# LLM Config
gpt4_config = {
    "cache_seed": 42,  # change the cache_seed for different trials
    "temperature": 0.1,
    "config_list": [{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "api_key": os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], "api_type": "openai"}],
    "timeout": 120,
}

# Agents
user_proxy = autogen.UserProxyAgent(
    name="Admin",
    system_message="A human admin. Interact with the planner to discuss the plan. Plan execution needs to be approved by this admin.",
    code_execution_config=False,
)
engineer = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="Software Engineer",
    llm_config=gpt4_config,
    system_message="""Software Engineer. You follow an approved plan. You write python/shell code to solve tasks. Wrap the code in a code block that specifies the script type. The user can't modify your code. So do not suggest incomplete code which requires others to modify. Don't use a code block if it's not intended to be executed by the executor.
Don't include multiple code blocks in one response. Do not ask others to copy and paste the result. Check the execution result returned by the executor.
If the result indicates there is an error, fix the error and output the code again. Suggest the full code instead of partial code or code changes. If the error can't be fixed or if the task is not solved even after the code is executed successfully, analyze the problem, revisit your assumption, collect additional info you need, and think of a different approach to try.
""",
)
scientist = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="Business Analyst",
    llm_config=gpt4_config,
    system_message="""Business Analyst. You follow an approved plan. You are experienced in analyzing companies and stocks. You don't write code.""",
)
planner = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="Planner",
    system_message="""Planner. Suggest a plan. Revise the plan based on feedback from admin and critic, until admin approval.
The plan may involve an software engineer who can write code and a business analyst who doesn't write code.
Explain the plan first. Be clear which step is performed by an software engineer, and which step is performed by a Business Analyst.
""",
    llm_config=gpt4_config,
)
executor = autogen.UserProxyAgent(
    name="Executor",
    system_message="Executor. Execute the code written by the engineer and report the result.",
    human_input_mode="NEVER",
    code_execution_config={
        "last_n_messages": 3,
        "work_dir": "work_dir",
        "use_docker": True,
    },
)
critic = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="Critic",
    system_message="Critic. Double check plan, claims, code from other agents and provide feedback. Check whether the plan includes adding verifiable info such as source URL.",
    llm_config=gpt4_config,
)
groupchat = autogen.GroupChat(
    agents=[user_proxy, engineer, scientist, planner, executor, critic], messages=[], max_round=50
)
manager = autogen.GroupChatManager(groupchat=groupchat, llm_config=gpt4_config)

# Start Chat
user_proxy.initiate_chat(
    manager,
    message="""
Create a sophisticated stock scoring system. Test it on the top 20 stocks.
"""
)
```

### Model Used

gpt-4o-mini

### Expected Behavior

No error

- **Verifiable Info:** Document the testing methodology and any historical data sources used for backtesting.

- **Verifiable Info:** Consider including a feedback loop from stakeholders or users of the scoring system to gather insights for adjustments.

#### 6. **Final Implementation**
- **Feedback:** Ensure that the implementation phase includes considerations for scalability and performance, especially if real-time data updates are involved.
- **Verifiable Info:** Document the technology stack and architecture that will be used for implementation.

#### 7. **Documentation and Reporting**
- **Feedback:** In addition to documenting the scoring system, consider creating user guides or tutorials for stakeholders who will use the system. This will enhance usability and understanding.
- **Verifiable Info:** Include a section in the documentation that cites all sources used in the development of the scoring system.

- Outline the scoring algorithm's logic.
- Define success criteria for testing and backtesting methodology.
- Establish a timeline for reviewing and adjusting criteria.
- Document the technology stack for implementation.
- Create user guides for better usability.

linked_prs.title: Add Validation for name in ConversableAgent to Prevent Whitespace
linked_prs.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please review https://docs.ag2.ai/docs/contributor-guide/contributing before opening a pull request. -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?
This PR adds regex-based validation to the ConversableAgent class to ensure the name attribute does not contain any whitespace. A ValueError with a clear message is raised if validation fails.

<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

## Related issue number
Closes #451 

<!-- For example: "Closes #1234" -->

## Checks

- [ ] I've included any doc changes needed for https://docs.ag2.ai/. See https://docs.ag2.ai/docs/contributor-guide/documentation to build and test documentation locally.
- [x] I've added tests (if relevant) corresponding to the changes introduced in this PR.
- [x] I've made sure all auto checks have passed.

ai_judgment.response: Yes. This is an agent issue because it involves an error related to LLM provider integration, specifically an `openai.BadRequestError` caused by an invalid parameter (`messages[6].name`) when invoking the OpenAI API. This aligns with the "Incompatible parameters to LLM providers" sub-category under "Incompatibility with LLM providers."
